question: Which of the following is NOT correctly matched? [Afonso de Albuquerque — Cities/Regions he captured or controlled]
options: Goa — Captured from the Bijapur Sultanate in 1510
Malacca — Conquered by Albuquerque in 1511 to control the spice trade route
Calicut — Captured and made the primary Portuguese base on the Malabar Coast by Albuquerque
Hormuz — Albuquerque captured this island city at the mouth of the Persian Gulf
wrong_fact: Albuquerque never captured Calicut. Calicut was ruled by the Zamorin who was hostile to the Portuguese. Albuquerque's main base on the Malabar Coast was Cochin (Kochi), not Calicut. He did conduct raids against Calicut but never held it.
explanation: Afonso de Albuquerque's conquests: Goa (1510, from Bijapur), Malacca (1511, controlling the Southeast Asian spice route), and Hormuz (1515, commanding the Persian Gulf). Cochin/Kochi was the first major Portuguese base on the Malabar Coast, friendly to Portugal. Calicut under the Zamorin was consistently anti-Portuguese and was never taken by Albuquerque.

question: Which of the following is NOT correctly matched? [Albuquerque — Strategic Importance of Captured Locations]
options: Hormuz — Controlled the entry to the Persian Gulf, choking off the overland and sea route of spices to Persia and Turkey
Malacca — Controlled the narrow strait between the Malay Peninsula and Sumatra, the gateway to the Spice Islands
Goa — Natural deep-water harbour on the west coast of India; ideal base for the Arabian Sea
Diu — Captured by Albuquerque in 1509 to dominate the Gujarat coast and northern Arabian Sea trade
wrong_fact: Diu was not captured by Albuquerque in 1509. The Battle of Diu (1509) was a naval battle off Diu where Albuquerque's predecessor Francisco de Almeida defeated the Egyptian-Calicut fleet. Diu itself was formally leased to Portugal only in 1535 under Governor Nuno da Cunha through a treaty with Gujarat's Bahadur Shah.
explanation: Albuquerque's three strategic captures — Goa, Malacca, and Hormuz — formed the triangle that dominated Indian Ocean trade. The Battle of Diu (1509) was a naval victory that destroyed the allied Muslim fleet but did not result in occupation of the city. Diu came under Portuguese control much later (1535). Albuquerque himself died in 1515 before Diu was ceded.

question: Which of the following is NOT correctly matched? [Albuquerque — Policies and Actions at Specific Locations]
options: Goa — Albuquerque encouraged intermarriage between Portuguese soldiers and local Hindu women to create a settled Christian community
Malacca — After conquest, Albuquerque built the fortress A Famosa to consolidate Portuguese control
Hormuz — Albuquerque made it a tributary state, extracting annual tribute from the local ruler
Aden — Albuquerque successfully blockaded and captured Aden in 1513, sealing the Red Sea trade route
wrong_fact: Albuquerque failed to capture Aden. His 1513 assault on Aden was repulsed. This failure was strategically significant because it left the Red Sea trade route (Egypt-Venice spice route) intact, which undermined the Portuguese monopoly on the spice trade.
explanation: Albuquerque's policy of intermarriage in Goa (Casados), construction of A Famosa fortress in Malacca, and making Hormuz a tribute-paying vassal are all well-documented. His failure at Aden in 1513 is equally significant — by not capturing this Red Sea gateway, the Portuguese could not fully strangle the alternative spice route, and Muslim merchants continued to use the Egypt-Red Sea route despite Portuguese pressure.
